items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:1:1
items.html:
The root of these kings is the first name BON: That is, in the world of correction they are the name HaVaYaH with the filling of Heys, which in Gematria is BON. And although in their source they are HaVaYaH of SAG, that is, the Nekudot of SAG, as the ARI writes in Etz Chaim, Gate 10, end of Chapter 3; study it there well: in the future, when all these kings are completely corrected, the name SAG will be restored to its former state and the name MA will be annulled, this being the matter of the world’s returning to chaos and void, and then there will be only the two lights of AB and SAG. End of quote. Even so, in the world of correction the Nekudot of SAG descended and became the name BON, which means the Nukva of the name MA and secondary to it, and all that she has she receives from the male, who is HaVaYaH of MA. Therefore we always call the ZAT of Nekudim by the name BON, even though they are the Nekudot of SAG.
Now in truth the Partzuf that emerged through the coupling on the screen of phase one, which is called the light of the Einayim, is discerned as HaVaYaH of MA, which means ten Sefirot at the level of ZA; yet it is called HaVaYaH of SAG for two reasons. First, because there is there the light of the male that emerged upon phase two of clothing, which is called YESHSUT, as above, page 404, in the Inner Light, the passage beginning “And it availed”; see there. And the level of YESHSUT is called HaVaYaH of SAG. The second reason is because of the vessels of Nekudim, which are the Nekudot of SAG of AK, that is, the nine lower ones of SAG that descended below the Tabur of AK, from which the light departed, and these vessels passed over to the ten Sefirot of the world of Nekudim, as written on page 428 in the Inner Light, the passage beginning “And one must.” They are therefore called the Nekudot of SAG.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:1:2
items.html: Every Malchut that exists in all the worlds was made from this name BON: For through the ascent of the lower Hey, who is Malchut, to the place of the Einayim, which is Hochma, Malchut was mingled and joined into each and every one of the ten Sefirot. And from then on this Malchut, joined with the first Hey, is found included in every Sefira and in every Partzuf, as written in the Inner Light, page 428, the passage beginning “Ten Nekudot.”
